The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Looking at this problem, I need to understand what happens when Mark repeatedly replaces pairs $(a, b)$ with $(\gcd(a,b), \text{lcm}(a,b))$ until no change occurs.

## Key Invariant

For each prime $p$, the **multiset of exponents** $\{v_p(n_1), v_p(n_2), \ldots, v_p(n_{2100})\}$ is preserved, since $\min(v_p(a), v_p(b))$ and $\max(v_p(a), v_p(b))$ replace $v_p(a)$ and $v_p(b)$.

## Final State

Mark stops when every pair is comparable under divisibility, meaning the final numbers form a **chain**: $n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_{2100}$.

Since exponents must be non-decreasing along the chain, the $i$-th number in the chain has:
$$v_p(n_i) = \text{the } i\text{-th smallest value in } \{v_p(1), v_p(2), \ldots, v_p(2100)\}$$

This **uniquely determines** the final state.

## Finding the 2026th Number

For each prime $p$, I count how many integers in $\{1,\ldots,2100\}$ have $v_p = 0$: that count is $2100 - \lfloor 2100/p \rfloor$.

**Primes with $v_p(n_{2026}) = 0$:** Need $2100 - \lfloor 2100/p \rfloor \geq 2026$, i.e., $\lfloor 2100/p\rfloor \leq 74$, giving $p \geq 29$.

**For relevant primes ($p < 29$), I compute cumulative counts:**

| $p$ | $v_p=0$ | cum. | $v_p=1$ | cum. | $v_p=2$ | cum. | $v_p=3$ | cum. | $v_p=4$ | cum. |
|-----|---------|------|---------|------|---------|------|---------|------|---------|------|
| 2 | 1050 | 1050 | 525 | 1575 | 263 | 1838 | 131 | 1969 | **66** | **2035** |
| 3 | 1400 | 1400 | 467 | 1867 | 156 | 2023 | **52** | **2075** | 17 | 2092 |
| 5 | 1680 | 1680 | 336 | 2016 | **68** | **2084** | 13 | 2097 | 3 | 2100 |
| 7 | 1800 | 1800 | 258 | **2058** | 36 | 2094 | 6 | 2100 | — | — |
| 11 | 1910 | 1910 | 173 | **2083** | 16 | 2099 | 1 | 2100 | — | — |
| 13 | 1939 | 1939 | 149 | **2088** | 12 | 2100 | — | — | — | — |
| 17 | 1977 | 1977 | 116 | **2093** | 7 | 2100 | — | — | — | — |
| 19 | 1990 | 1990 | 105 | **2095** | 5 | 2100 | — | — | — | — |
| 23 | 2009 | 2009 | 88 | **2097** | 3 | 2100 | — | — | — | — |

Reading off the exponent at position 2026 (bolded ranges contain 2026):

$$n_{2026} = 2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7^1 \cdot 11^1 \cdot 13^1 \cdot 17^1 \cdot 19^1 \cdot 23^1$$

## Computing the Number of Divisors

$$\tau(n_{2026}) = (4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6 = 5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 64 = \boxed{3840}$$
